Architecture

The platform at a glance

An enterprise healthcare product built as Spring Boot microservices with Angular web clients. Services own their data in PostgreSQL or MongoDB and share events through Apache Kafka. Each service keeps HTTP handling, business logic and data access in separate layers.

Backend
Java, Spring Boot, Spring Security, JPA / Hibernate
Frontend
Angular, TypeScript
Data
PostgreSQL, MongoDB
Integration
REST APIs, Apache Kafka events
Testing
JUnit 5 and Mockito, Jasmine and Karma, Playwright for end-to-end
Delivery
Git-based merge requests, CI pipelines, staged environments

Team-built platform · my contributions

Workflow engine

The engine that runs configurable business processes and approvals across the platform.

The challenge

Hospital operations depend on multi-step processes, such as approvals and hand-offs between departments, that differ from one customer to the next. Hard-coding each one doesn’t scale.

My contribution

Worked on the workflow engine that executes configurable processes, including sequential and parallel execution, state transitions and approval flows.

What it covers

  • Configurable processes and approval flows instead of hard-coded steps.
  • Sequential execution, where each step starts only after the previous one finishes.
  • Parallel execution, where independent steps run together and the workflow continues once they have all finished.
  • Explicit state transitions so every workflow instance is always in a known state.

Technologies

  • Java
  • Spring Boot
  • Angular
  • Microservices
  • REST APIs

Sequential vs. parallel execution

Sequential
Order is guaranteed, so a step can rely on the output of the one before it. It’s simpler to reason about and recover, but the total time is the sum of every step.
Parallel
Independent steps run at the same time, which shortens the overall flow. In exchange, the engine has to join the branches, decide what happens when one fails, and keep shared state consistent.
Choosing
Steps with data dependencies stay sequential; independent approvals or notifications can branch. Making that a configuration choice keeps the engine general.

Procurement management

The purchasing lifecycle, from request for quotation to rate contracts and approvals.

The challenge

Hospital purchasing runs through several stages and approvals, and each stage feeds stock, billing and accounts downstream.

My contribution

Worked on procurement capabilities across the purchasing lifecycle.

What it covers

  • Request for quotation (RFQ) and quotation management.
  • Rate contracts for agreed supplier pricing.
  • Approval workflows built on the platform’s workflow engine.
  • Integration with inventory so purchases flow into stock.

Technologies

  • Java
  • Spring Boot
  • Angular
  • PostgreSQL
  • Apache Kafka

Inventory management

Stock, items and unit conversions, with indent and return flows connected to procurement.

The challenge

Items are bought in one unit and issued in another, and stock moves between stores and departments. Quantities have to stay correct at every step.

My contribution

Worked on inventory operations and their integration with procurement and other modules.

What it covers

  • Stock and item management.
  • Unit-of-measure conversions between purchase and issue units.
  • Indent (internal request) and return flows.
  • Integration with procurement, billing and clinical modules, including consumption of non-stock items.

Technologies

  • Java
  • Spring Boot
  • Angular
  • PostgreSQL
  • Apache Kafka
